brief.title: Active Satellites in Earth Orbit — 2026 Catalog Analysis
brief.one_liner: A comprehensive analytical report on the 14,875 active satellites currently orbiting Earth, examining constellation composition, orbital regime distribution, and key orbital characteristics.
brief.goal: Provide the reader with a clear, data-driven picture of the current satellite population: who operates the most satellites, how they are distributed across orbital regimes (LEO/MEO/GEO/HEO), what the dominant orbital parameters look like, and what trends in launch activity and constellation growth can be inferred from the catalog.

required_sections.title: Catalog Overview & Key Figures
required_sections.objective: Summarize the total satellite count, data freshness (EPOCH range), and high-level statistics such as mean motion, inclination, and eccentricity distributions.

required_sections.title: Orbital Regime Classification
required_sections.objective: Classify satellites into LEO, MEO, GEO, and HEO categories using MEAN_MOTION thresholds and present the count and share of each regime.

required_sections.title: Major Constellation & Operator Breakdown
required_sections.objective: Identify the largest satellite constellations (e.g., Starlink, OneWeb, GPS) by parsing OBJECT_NAME prefixes, and quantify their share of the total population.

required_sections.title: Launch Year Trends
required_sections.objective: Extract launch year from OBJECT_ID and analyze the historical growth curve of currently active satellites, highlighting recent acceleration.

required_sections.title: Orbital Parameter Deep Dive
required_sections.objective: Examine distributions of INCLINATION, ECCENTRICITY, and MEAN_MOTION to characterize the most common orbital shells and highlight outliers (e.g., highly eccentric or polar orbits).

required_sections.title: Key Takeaways & Outlook
required_sections.objective: Synthesize findings into actionable insights regarding orbital congestion, constellation dominance, and implications for space sustainability.
